findings.location: README.md discipline paragraph (line 20) vs Heterogeneous-provider config (lines 36-39)
findings.evidence: Line 20 states the heterogeneous review ring runs as an out-of-process subprocess '(default `claude -p`; qwen3/bigmodel/minimax via profiles)'. Lines 36-39 of the SAME doc state the opposite: 'The upstream `claude -p` mechanism survives ONLY as an explicitly labeled external-harness opt-in ... it is never the default.' The authoritative source disagrees with line 20 too: hetero_review.py:989 sets `default=os.environ.get("HETERO_PROFILE", "pi-ai")` and hetero_doc_review.py:1028 sets `default=...("HETERO_DOC_PROFILE", "pi-ai")`. So line 20 contradicts both line 39 and the live argparse default.
findings.suggestion: Change line 20's '(default `claude -p`)' to '(default DSH-native pi-ai substrate; claude -p is the external-harness opt-in)' to match lines 36-39 and the code.

findings.evidence: README line 53 instructs 'python3 $SOLIDFORGE_PRESET_ROOT/skills/parallel-development/infra/install/arm.py <project>' and arm-tools.md:15 invokes 'python3 "${SOLIDFORGE_PRESET_ROOT}/skills/parallel-development/infra/install/arm.py"', treating $SOLIDFORGE_PRESET_ROOT as a live variable. But a repo-wide search for any assignment (`SOLIDFORGE_PRESET_ROOT=` or `export SOLIDFORGE_PRESET_ROOT`) across scripts/, preset/, plugins/ returns ZERO matches. scripts/install.sh installs to `$DEST` (= $DSH_HOME/.agent-presets/solidforge) and never exports SOLIDFORGE_PRESET_ROOT. The variable is load-bearing for the entire Layer-2 arming flow yet nothing in the install path sets it.
findings.suggestion: Either have install.sh export SOLIDFORGE_PRESET_ROOT=$DEST (and document it), or state in the README how a session obtains it (DSH preset-env injection), since the command file assumes it is already in the environment.

findings.evidence: The committed, portable README embeds an author-machine runtime note: '*(this workspace is armed: `HETERO_PROFILE=zhipu,minimax` — GLM-5.2 + MiniMax-M3, both DSH-native routes)*'. This both (a) contradicts the same section's own stated default ('the DSH-native default ... profiles/pi-ai.json'), and (b) bakes the current maintainer's local profile selection into an install doc that every reader is expected to follow — a non-portable workspace secret leaking into a committed artifact.
findings.suggestion: Remove the parenthetical workspace-armed note from the committed README; record such runtime state in a gitignored per-workspace file instead.

findings.evidence: Line 59 says: 'pipe a payload into `infra/hooks/fast_gate.py` / `blueprint_guard.py`'. The shorthand `infra/hooks/` resolves nowhere from the repo root; the real paths are preset/skills/parallel-development/infra/hooks/fast_gate.py and preset/skills/parallel-development/infra/hooks/blueprint_guard.py (verified). This is the identical shorthand-rooted citation defect the primary reviewer caught for arm.py in the same-doc skills/arm-tools tables, but on a different line (Verify section) it went uncovered.
findings.suggestion: Write the full path 'preset/skills/parallel-development/infra/hooks/fast_gate.py' (and blueprint_guard.py) in line 59.

findings.evidence: The README's single hetero-config narrative covers only the shared/pd substrate (PI_AI_API_KEY, HETERO_PROFILE) and never names HETERO_DOC_PROFILE, the separate selector the csr doc-leg reads. The committed .env.solidforge.example:25 explicitly documents the split ('HETERO_DOC_PROFILE=pi-ai # csr's separate selector (same rule)') and hetero_doc_review.py:1028 reads HETERO_DOC_PROFILE as an independent knob. A reader of the README alone cannot arm csr's different-family leg. I could not independently verify the claim that the two selectors are truly independent at runtime — flagging that as the coverage boundary of this check.
findings.suggestion: Add one line to the hetero-config section noting csr uses HETERO_DOC_PROFILE (same rule, separate var) so the doc leg is arming-complete from the README.

findings.location: README.md skills row line 11 ('Agent preset' table cell)
findings.evidence: Line 11 describes the composition as 'standard coding-agent rows + SolidForge persona + preset-local skills', implying the agent.cordis.yml composition itself defines skills. The actual source (agent.cordis.yml skill-filesystem row) only mounts a customSkillDirs entry pointing at the `skills/` directory; the five skills are filesystem-loaded via the dsh-skill-filesystem host service, not defined as composition rows. The phrase 'preset-local skills' mislocates where the skills live relative to the composition.
findings.suggestion: Re-word to '+ skills mounted from preset/skills/ via customSkillDirs' to match what the composition actually does.

findings.location: README.md line 20 (discipline paragraph) vs lines 30-39 (install section)
findings.evidence: README line 20: 'the heterogeneous review ring runs as an out-of-process, cross-provider subprocess (default `claude -p`; qwen3/bigmodel/minimax via profiles).' README line 32-33: 'the DSH-native default substrate spawns a fresh, stateless `dsh --profile headless` subprocess whose throwaway `DSH_HOME` pins a DIFFERENT provider/model route (`substrate: dsh`, `profiles/pi-ai.json`...)'. Cross-check: preset/skills/parallel-development/references/install.md line 101 confirms 'DSH-NATIVE default: `dsh --profile headless`'. The discourse paragraph's leading claim is the upstream default; the install paragraph's leading claim is the current DSH default — the two are conflated under a single unlabeled 'default' in the discourse paragraph, and a reader landing in the discourse paragraph first will read it as the current default being `claude -p`.
findings.suggestion: rephrase the discipline paragraph to lead with the DSH-native default (dsh --profile headless) and explicitly tag the `claude -p` reference as the upstream mechanism it re-derives

findings.evidence: README lines 43-45 list: '1. <preset-root>/.env.solidforge — the DSH site default ... 2. <project>/.env; 3. <project>/.env.solidforge — the arm-tools-provisioned file (authoritative among files)' under the heading 'Credentials resolve in highest-precedence-first order (setdefault — first-loaded wins...)'. Actual code: `_load_dotenv_file(os.path.join(root, '.env.solidforge'))` then `_load_dotenv_file(os.path.join(root, '.env'))` then `_load_dotenv_file(os.path.join(preset, '.env.solidforge'))` — i.e. project/.env.solidforge wins, preset-root/.env.solidforge is the last fallback. The README's 'highest-precedence-first' table is the OPPOSITE precedence of the code. The committed preset root hosts `.env.solidforge.example` (line 6) which carries the same reversed ordering, so the example file documents the wrong precedence too.
findings.suggestion: swap the numbered list order to project/.env.solidforge → project/.env → preset-root/.env.solidforge (= match the code's load_dotenv order); or rephrase the README's preamble as 'lowest-precedence-first' so the listed order matches the code's actual precedence

findings.location: previous finding 'outcome-axis-count' (round 1) — the finding targets the README, but the README text is correct; the finding's own claim is inverted
findings.evidence: README line 12: 'the document-convergence layer (csr — process-axis), and the two outcome-axis verifiers (psv/pas)'. Verified against the cited sources: csr SKILL.md frontmatter says 'Out: ... outcome-axis judgment (human)' and section 'Process-axis, not outcome-axis' (line 18-20) explicitly states 'the skill converges a doc's PROCESS-AXIS quality'. psv SKILL.md frontmatter says 'Does NOT judge whether the doc is RIGHT (outcome-axis — human)' and line 11: 'It opens the OUTCOME axis's admissible surface that cross-source-review (csr) cannot reach'. pas SKILL.md line 19: 'prior-art-search lives entirely on the outcome axis'. The previous reviewer's claim that the README 'classified csr as an outcome-axis verifier while csr SKILL.md declares process-axis' is exactly inverted — the README correctly maps csr→process-axis and psv/pas→outcome-axis. reclassifying csr as 'the convergence layer' would be the wrong direction.
findings.suggestion: drop this finding — the README's axis assignment is correct as stated; the previous reviewer inverted the claim

findings.evidence: README line 59: 'Gate behavior: pipe a payload into `infra/hooks/fast_gate.py` / `blueprint_guard.py` (see `references/hooks-reference.md`).' The cited `references/hooks-reference.md` is a relative path; from the repo root there is no top-level `references/` directory (verified: `find . -maxdepth 2 -name references -type d` does not return a repo-root match). The actual file is at `preset/skills/parallel-development/references/hooks-reference.md`. The reader has to know which skill's `references/` is intended; the README does not disambiguate. The prior same-family reviewer's analogous `probe-plugin-pointer` finding (for `test/verification.md`) flagged the same kind of unspecified-relpath issue but only for one of the two links here — the second one was missed.
findings.suggestion: write the full path `preset/skills/parallel-development/references/hooks-reference.md` (matching the table-row convention used at line 14); the gate-script paths on the same line have the same relative-path ambiguity and could be qualified similarly

findings.location: README.md row 4 (Structural plugins) — the README claims the dynamic Cordis plugins are the new DSH enforcement, but the actual plugin source files still carry the pre-redesign substrate default
findings.evidence: README row 4 (line 15) presents plugins/loop-gates.host.js, plugins/run-record.host.js, plugins/hetero-review.host.js as the new DSH enforcement; the README's install section (line 32-39) declares the DSH-native default substrate as `dsh --profile headless`. (default `claude -p` native; qwen3 / bigmodel / minimax via profiles/<backend>.json) as a fresh, stateless session.' plugins/hetero-review.host.js line 34 (the registered tool's description): '...
